BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r6.claim: A conjecturer is a liar even when his guess happens to be true, since it was made without knowledge, reliable probability, or report; these conjecturers are liars who assert what has no basis.
BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r6.anchor: كل قول مقول عن ظن وتخمين يقال له خرص سواء كان ذلك مطابقا للشيء

BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r7.claim: ‘In a ghamra’ means engulfed in ignorance and misguidance that conceals the afterlife; ‘sahun’ adds that they neglect what they were commanded.
BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r7.anchor: غمرة} من الجهل والضلال تغمرهم وتغشاهم عن أمر الآخرة

BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r8.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r8.claim: Al-Raghib says sahw is error from inadvertence: what was not produced by one’s actions is excused, whereas conduct generated by one’s own act is accountable and is the condemned kind here.
BURSEVI:v9p122#2/r8.anchor: قال الراغب : السهو خطأ عن غفلة وذلك ضربان أحدهما أن لا يكون

QASHANI:51:8-13/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:51:8-13/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:51:8-13/r4.claim: The “reckoners” are cursed liars whose ignorance engulfs them; they are heedless of perfection and requital.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3311#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3311#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3311#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that those lost in heedlessness persist in neglecting their prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3311#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : الذين هم في غمرة ساهون يقول : في صلاتهم يتمادون

NAHHAS:v4p235/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p235/r21.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p235/r21.claim: الذين is nominative as an adjective to الخراصين and as the start of a clause whose predicate ساهون lies within the relative clause; outside the Quran, ساهين can be accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
NAHHAS:v4p235/r21.anchor: ( الذين ) في موضع رفع نعت للخراصين وهي مبتدأ و ( ساهون ) خبره والجملة في الصلة وفي غير القرآن يجوز نصب ساهين

NAHHAS:v4p235/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p235/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p235/r22.claim: A غمرة is a covering of falsehood and ignorance, by analogy with a person or water that covers whoever enters it.
NAHHAS:v4p235/r22.anchor: ( في غمرة ) أي في تغطية الباطل والجهل ومنه فلان غمر وماء غمر يغطي من دخله

NAHHAS:v4p235/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p235/r23.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v4p235/r23.claim: Ibn Zayd says they are heedless of what God revealed and of his commands and prohibitions.
NAHHAS:v4p235/r23.anchor: قال ابن زيد ساهون عن ما أنزله الله وعن أمره ونهيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p173/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p173/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p173/r6.claim: غَمْرة is what envelops and covers a person, like deep water; here it is the covering of ignorance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p173/r6.anchor: والغمرة: ما يغشى الإنسان ويغطيه كغمرة الماء، والمعنى في غمرة من الجهالة.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p173/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p173/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p173/r7.claim: The heedless are unaware of their immersion in ignorance and other avenues for reflection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p173/r7.anchor: و: ساهون معناه عن أنهم في غمرة وعن غير ذلك من وجوه النظر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p30#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p30#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p30#2/r1.claim: Those in a “deep immersion” are blind and ignorant about the afterlife; “heedless” means inattentive, with the heart turning away from something.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p30#2/r1.anchor: أي في عمى وجهالة بأمر الآخرة ساهون أي غافلون والسهو الغفلة عن الشيء وذهاب القلب عنه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p415#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p415#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وغير واحد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p415#3/r1.claim: Those heedless in the deluge are lost in disbelief and doubt, inattentive and unmindful.

JISHUMI:v9p6584/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6584/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6584/r4.claim: The description “in a flood, heedless” shows that knowledge is acquired.
JISHUMI:v9p6584/r4.anchor: ويدل قوله: (في غمرة ساهون) أن المعارف مكتسبة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p400#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p400#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p400#2/r4.claim: Fi ghamrah means submerged in ignorance, while sahun means heedless of what they were commanded.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p400#2/r4.anchor: فى غمرة } في جهل يغمرهم { ساهون } غافلون عما أمروا به

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r24.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r24.claim: They are heedless and distracted in heedlessness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r24.anchor: في غفلة لاهون , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r25.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r25.claim: A second report from him says they persist in their misguidance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r25.anchor: في ضلالاتهم متمادون , وهو مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r26.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r26.claim: He describes them as wandering in blindness and doubt.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r26.anchor: في عمى وشبهة يترددون , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r27.claim: Possibly they are immersed in sinful acts and neglect their obligations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p362/r27.anchor: في مأثم المعاصي ساهون عن أداء الفرائض

MUJAHID:v2p616#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p616#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p616#4/r1.claim: He compares the heart of the heedless person to a quiver.
MUJAHID:v2p616#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ في غمرة ساهون ﴾ يقول قلبه في مثل كنانة

MUQATIL:51:7-12/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:51:7-12/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:51:7-12/r4.claim: The cursed conjecturers are seventeen liars whom al-Walid b. al-Mughira sent in groups of four to festival roads to call Muhammad sorcerer, madman, poet, soothsayer, and liar; distracted, they mockingly ask when Judgment comes.
MUQATIL:51:7-12/r4.anchor: وكانوا سبعة عشر رجلا، فقال لهم الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي: لينطلق كل أربعة منكم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p177#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p177#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p177#2/r1.claim: The heedless are submerged in ignorance and inattentive to what they were commanded.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p177#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ الذين هم في غمرة ﴾ في جهل يغمرهم ﴿ ساهون ﴾ غافلون عما امروا به

QURTUBI-FULL:51:9-11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:9-11/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:51:9-11/r10.claim: Ghamrah is what covers and overwhelms; the people described are heedless and distracted from the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:9-11/r10.anchor: الغمرة ما ستر الشيء وغطاه. ومنه نهر غمر

QURTUBI-FULL:51:9-11/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:9-11/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:51:9-11/r11.claim: Sāhūn means heedless and unmindful of the hereafter.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:9-11/r11.anchor: «ساهون» أي لاهون غافلون عن أمر الآخرة.

RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r1.claim: Grammatically, sāhūn may be a second predicate of “they,” so both being immersed and being heedless describe them.
RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر ، والمبتدأ هو قوله : { هم }

RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r2.claim: Alternatively, sāhūn is the predicate and “in an immersion” specifies the setting of their heedlessness; the phrase allows a definite subject to take a clause as predicate.
RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون { ساهون } خبرا و { فى غمرة } ظرف له

RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r4.claim: The added description “heedless” after “in an immersion” shows that they fell into ignorance and falsehood, forgot themselves, and did not turn back.
RAZI-FULL:v28p170#4/r4.anchor: يفيد أنهم وقعوا في جهل وباطل ونسوا أنفسهم

STUDYQURAN:51:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:11/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:51:11/r1.claim: The conjecturers wander in stupefying ignorance.
STUDYQURAN:51:11/r1.anchor: The conjecturers roam about in stupefying ignorance (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:51:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:11/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:51:11/r2.claim: They are heedless of their coming fate and of what God commanded them to do.
STUDYQURAN:51:11/r2.anchor: heedless of what is to befall them and of what God has commanded them to do (Ṭ)

TAB-FULL:v21p494/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r1.claim: They persist in an overpowering deluge of error and are heedless of the truth brought by Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r1.anchor: في غمرة الضلالة وغلبتها عليهم متمادون

TAB-FULL:v21p494/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says they persist in their misguidance and, in another gloss, are heedlessly distracted.
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {الذين هم في غمرة ساهون} [الذاريات: 11] يقول: «في ضلالتهم يتمادون»

TAB-FULL:v21p494/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r3.claim: Qatada interprets their state as delusion and doubt.
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {الذين هم في غمرة ساهون} [الذاريات: 11] يقول: «في غمرة وشبهة»

TAB-FULL:v21p494/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says they are heedless of what came to them, was revealed, and God commanded; he compares it to hearts submerged in 23:63.
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {في غمرة ساهون} [الذاريات: 11] قال: " ساهون عما أتاهم، وعما نزل عليهم

TAB-FULL:v21p494/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r5.claim: Mujahid says the heart is enclosed in a covering.
TAB-FULL:v21p494/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، {في غمرة ساهون} [الذاريات: 11] : «قلبه في كنانة»

TABATABAI:51:9-12/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:9-12/r8.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:51:9-12/r8.claim: Ghamra is a great body of water covering its bed, used metaphorically for ignorance engulfing someone; sahun is said to mean general heedlessness.
TABATABAI:51:9-12/r8.anchor: الغمرة - كما ذكر الراغب - معظم الماء الساتر لمقرها، وجعل مثلا

TABATABAI:51:9-12/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:9-12/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:9-12/r9.claim: The conjecturers are submerged in ignorance and heedless of the truth of what they have been told.
TABATABAI:51:9-12/r9.anchor: ومعنى الآية وهي تصف الخراصين الذين هم في جهالة أحاطت بهم غافلون عن حقيقة ما أخبروا به

TABRISI:51:10-14/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:10-14/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:51:10-14/r5.claim: The deniers are enveloped in confusion and heedlessness, overcome by ignorance and inattentive to what they owe God.

TABRISI:51:10-14/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:10-14/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:51:10-14/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes them as persisting in misguidance.
TABRISI:51:10-14/r6.anchor: هم في ضلالتهم متمادون عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:51:10-14/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:10-14/r7.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:51:10-14/r7.claim: Qatāda describes them as wandering blindly.

TABRISI:51:10-14/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:10-14/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:51:10-14/r8.claim: Another account orders ignorance's stages as inattention, heedlessness, then confusion, making confusion extreme ignorance of truth and fate.
TABRISI:51:10-14/r8.anchor: أول مراتب الجهل السهو ثم الغفلة ثم الغمرة

THALABI:v9p110/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p110/r17.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p110/r17.claim: The heedless are immersed in doubt and distraction.
THALABI:v9p110/r17.anchor: الذين هم في غمرة: شبهة وغفلة ساهون: لا هون.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r1.claim: Ghamra is something that submerges and covers; it can describe a river that overwhelms whoever enters, and the expression also occurs for the throes of death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r1.anchor: الغمرة ما غمر الشيء فغطاه. يقال: هذا نهر غمر. أي يغمر فيه من دخله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they are blind and ignorant of the afterlife, heedless and distracted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r2.anchor: في عمى وجهالة عن أمر الآخرة ساهون لاهون غافلون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r3.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r3.claim: In Arabic, sahw means inattentiveness and the heart’s losing track of something; al-Layth records the usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p433/r3.anchor: ومعنى السهو في اللغة الغفلة عن الشيء، وذهاب القلب عنه. يقال: سها يسهو سهوا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:9-16/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:9-16/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:9-16/r3.claim: Those immersed in heedlessness are distracted and careless.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:9-16/r3.anchor: الذين هم في غمرة } غفلة { ساهون } لاهون

ELMALILI:51:1-23#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:51:1-23#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:51:1-23#2/r13.claim: They are heedless inside an engulfing torrent-like swamp, stupor, drunkenness, or ignorance, unaware of God and the disaster coming to them.
ELMALILI:51:1-23#2/r13.anchor: müstevlî bir sel gibi kendilerini her noktadan sarıp bürümüş olan bir batak, bir sarhoşluk veya bir cehalet içinde

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p471/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p471/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p471/r4.claim: Those absorbed in heedlessness and wild conjecture are the ones who have lost their senses and dare to doubt the certainty of the warning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p471/r4.anchor: Only those who have lost their senses are daring to doubt their certainty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p478/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p478/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p478/r4.claim: The description of those immersed in heedlessness is also a sentence of scolding and rebuke.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p478/r4.anchor: This sentence is also meant to scold and rebuke them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p479/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p479/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p479/r4.claim: The opening words of 51:11 describe people who have abandoned divine light because they are engulfed by their own desires and conjectures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p479/r4.anchor: state an attribute of those who use their whims and conjecture

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p480/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p480/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p480/r1.claim: Ghamrah is the darkness of base desire and worldly greed; sāhūn is an additional predicate emphasizing their continuing negligence and refusal to wake from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p480/r1.anchor: refers to the darkness of one’s base desires and greed for this world

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p550/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p550/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p550/r6.claim: They are submerged in ignorance and heedless of what they were commanded.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p550/r6.anchor: في غمرة: في جهل يغمرهم، ساهون: غافلون عن ما أمروا به.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p6#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p6#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p6#2/r1.claim: A “deep” state is profound ignorance that envelops people like water covering what lies within it; heedlessness means being inattentive to what they were commanded, broadly any negligence.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p6#2/r1.anchor: غافلون عما أمروا به فالمراد بالسهو مطلق الغفلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p372#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p372#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p372#2/r3.claim: Ghamra means heedlessness, blindness, and ignorance; sahun means heedless of the afterlife, the heart's attention having gone from it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p372#2/r3.anchor: {الذين هم في غمرة} غفلة وعمى وجهالة، {ساهون} لاهون غافلون عن أمر الآخرة،

BAYDAWI-FULL:51:10-16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:10-16/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:10-16/r2.claim: The people are submerged in ignorance and heedless of what they were commanded.
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:10-16/r2.anchor: في جهل يغمرهم. { سهون } غافلون عما أمروا به

BIQAI-FULL:v7p273/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p273/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p273/r3.claim: Those in a ‘deep immersion’ are submerged in blindness, error, intoxication, and ignorance, as unstable as someone walking in the open sea; their speech, conduct, and states are disordered.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p273/r3.anchor: أي أعماق من العمى والضلال , غارقون في سكرهم وجهلهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p273/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p273/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p273/r4.claim: The heedless are forgetful, distracted, bewildered, and pulled away from what matters, displaying conflicting dispositions under distress.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p273/r4.anchor: أي عريقون في السهو وهو النسيان والغفلة والحيرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r1.claim: The author notes that 23:63 says their hearts are submerged, unlike 51:11 which says they are in a state of heedlessness; naming hearts matters because the heart is the locus of humility and cannot be humble while engulfed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r1.anchor: كما قال في مكان آخر من القرآن الكريم (الذاريات 11) بل قال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r2.claim: The people who give what they give while fearing their return to God have hearts marked by awe, a quality associated with humility; the disbelievers’ submerged hearts prevent it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r2.anchor: والوجَلُ أمرٌ قلبي وهو من لوازم الخشوع أيضاً. وذكرُ الكفار وذمهم بقوله: {بَلْ قُلُوبُهُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r3.claim: Their failure to submit or supplicate to their Lord means they lack humility, since the humble person is submissive, pleading, and abject before God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r3.anchor: فلم يخشعوا، لأن الخاشع مستكين لربه متضرع متذلل إليه.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r4.claim: Arrogance and being high-handed contradict humility, which consists of lowering oneself and submitting to God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r4.anchor: وقال: {فاستكبروا وَكَانُواْ قَوْماً عَالِينَ} والاستكبارُ والعُلوُّ مناقضان للخشوع، إذ الخشوع، تَطَامنٌ وتَذلُّلٌ وخضوعٌ لله رب العالمين.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r5.claim: Beginning al-Muʾminūn with humility suits the sūra’s atmosphere, and it begins with the quality reported to disappear first and ends with prayer, reported to disappear last.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r5.anchor: فبدأ بما يُرفع أولاً، وختم بما يرفع آخراً، وهو الصلاة،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r6.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r6.claim: ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit says that a time will soon come when one enters the mosque and sees no man there who is humble.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r6.anchor: وقد جاء عن عبادة بن الصامت أنه قال: "يوشك أن تدخل المسجد، فلا ترى فيه رجلاً خاشعاً".

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r7.speaker: حذيفة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r7.claim: Ḥudhayfa says humility will be the first thing lost from religion and prayer the last, as Islam’s bonds are undone one by one.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p131/r7.anchor: وعن حذيفة أنه قال: "أولُ ما تَفقدون من دينكم الخشوع، وآخرُ ما تفقدون من دينكم الصلاة

ITQAN:v2p331/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p331/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p331/r2.claim: They persist in their misguidance, heedless.
ITQAN:v2p331/r2.anchor: 1969 ﴿ في غمرة ساهون ﴾ في ضلالتهم يتمادون 1970 ﴿ يفتنون ﴾ يعذبون
